name: Wunderkammer Elbigenalp
kurzbeschreibung: The Wunderkammer in Elbigenalp: award-winning museum in the birthplace of the Geierwally dedicated to Johann Anton Falger, Lechtal lithography, and alpine history.
beschreibung:
Overview

The extraordinary Wunderkammer Elbigenalp (frequently referred to as the Falger-Museum) is located in the historic main village of the Tyrolean Lechtal in the municipality of Elbigenalp (Reutte district) at Dorfstraße 44, at an altitude of around 1,039 metres. Renowned as the home village of the legendary "Geierwally" (Anna Stainer-Knittel) and the centre of traditional Lechtal woodcarving, the municipality created a multi-award-winning modern cultural museum in the heritage-protected birthplace of polymath Johann Anton Falger. Conceived in the tradition of baroque cabinets of curiosities, the museum unites natural history, the history of science, folk art, and the poignant fate of the Lechtal Schwabenkinder.

Route & Requirements

Its namesake Johann Anton Falger (1791–1876) was an outstanding artist, cartographer, lithographer, and passionate collector who decisively shaped the cultural identity of the Lechtal. The exhibition showcases a fascinating wealth of original exhibits: from hand-drawn topographical maps of the Lechtaler Alpen and rare mineral and fossil discoveries to delicate lithographic prints and anatomical preparations. Another major focus is dedicated to the painter Anna Stainer-Knittel: original oil paintings, drawings, and personal letters document the emancipated life of this fearless artist who, as a young woman in 1863, was lowered down a sheer rock face on a rope to clear an eagle's nest, inspiring the famous novel. Deeply moving is the section addressing the phenomenon of the Schwabenkinder: for centuries, bitter poverty in the Lechtal compelled impoverished mountain farming families to send their children on foot across snow-covered alpine passes each spring to Upper Swabia to work as seasonal farmhands and shepherd boys. Historical travel diaries, photographs, and documentary films illuminate this chapter of alpine social history.

Visit & Arrival

The Wunderkammer Elbigenalp is open from late May to late October and from mid-December to mid-April, Wednesday through Sunday from 14:00 to 18:00 (closed on Mondays and Tuesdays; group tours available year-round by advance reservation). Admission prices (2025/2026 season): adults approx. €6.00, seniors approx. €5.00, children and youths (6 to 15 years) approx. €3.00, young children free; family ticket approx. €14.00. Holders of the regional Lechtal Aktiv Card receive discounted admission. Getting there by car: via the B198 (Lechtalstraße) from Reutte or from the Arlberg directly to Elbigenalp; free parking is available in the village centre near the municipal office (Gemeindeamt) or at the woodcarving school (Schnitzschule). By public transport: train to Reutte in Tirol station, from where Postbus line 110 runs at frequent intervals directly to the Elbigenalp Gemeindeamt stop (only a two-minute walk).

Tips

The museum is largely barrier-free and accessible for wheelchair users via a modern elevator. Be sure to take time to experience the audio stations playing original dialect recordings in the unmistakable Lechtal vernacular. After your visit, a village tour to the renowned vocational school for applied arts (Schnitzschule Elbigenalp) and a detour to the Geierwally-Freilichtbühne in the wildly romantic Bernhardstalschlucht gorge are highly recommended.
